review.plain: Wilfully and maliciously burning a dwelling house, or a building next to one or whose burning burns one, or helping do so, is punishable by up to 20 years in state prison.
acts: sets fire to, burns, or causes to be burned
aids, counsels or procures the burning of, a dwelling house

intent: Wilfully and maliciously
terms: "Dwelling house": all buildings used as dwellings such as apartment houses, tenement houses, hotels, boarding houses, dormitories, hospitals, institutions, sanatoria, or other buildings where persons are domiciled

penalties.penalty: Up to 20 years in state prison, or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction, or a fine of up to $10,000, or both such fine and imprisonment

crimes.act: Sets fire to, burns, or causes to be burned, or aids, counsels or procures the burning of, a dwelling house, or a building adjoining or adjacent to a dwelling house, or a building by the burning whereof a dwelling house is burned
ways: aids, counsels or procures the burning of
conditions: Applies whether the dwelling house or other building is the property of himself or another
Applies whether the same is occupied or unoccupied

review.plain: Wilfully and maliciously burning a church, public building, business building, vessel, vehicle, bridge, or other building or structure not a dwelling, or helping do so, is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: sets fire to, burns, or causes to be burned
aids, counsels or procures the burning of, a meeting house

penalties.penalty: Up to 10 years in state prison or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction

crimes.act: Sets fire to, burns, or causes to be burned, or aids, counsels or procures the burning of, a meeting house, church, court house, town house, college, academy, jail or other building erected for public use, or a banking house, warehouse, store, manufactory, mill, barn, stable, shop, outhouse or other building, or an office building, lumber yard, ship, vessel, street car or railway car, or a bridge, lock, dam, flume, tank, or any building or structure or contents thereof
ways: aids, counsels or procures the burning of
conditions: The building or structure is not included or described in the preceding section
Applies whether the same is the property of himself or of another
Applies whether occupied, unoccupied or vacant

review.plain: Wilfully and maliciously burning wood, lumber, crops, trees, fences, another's personal property worth over $25, or any boat or motor vehicle, or helping do so, is punishable by up to 3 years in state prison.

terms: "Motor vehicle": as defined in section one of chapter ninety

penalties.penalty: Up to 3 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $500 and up to 1 year in a jail or house of correction

ways: otherwise destroys or injures by burning
causes to be burned or otherwise so destroyed or injured
aids, counsels or procures the burning of

A boat, motor vehicle or other conveyance may be of himself or another

review.plain: Wilfully and maliciously attempting to burn any building, structure or property covered by the preceding arson sections, helping in the attempt, or doing any preliminary act, is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison.

aids, counsels or assists in such an attempt to set fire to or burn
commits any act preliminary thereto or in furtherance thereof

intent: Wilfully and maliciously
terms: "Attempt to burn": the placing or distributing of any flammable, explosive or combustible material or substance or any device in or against any building, structure or property mentioned in the foregoing sections in an arrangement or preparation with intent eventually to wilfully and maliciously set fire to or burn it, or to procure the setting fire to or burning of the same

penalties.penalty: Up to 10 years in state prison, or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction, or a fine of up to $1,000

commits any act preliminary thereto or in furtherance thereof
conditions: The target is a building, structure or property mentioned in the foregoing sections

crimes.act: Cuts or removes a bell rope or a wire or conduit connected with a fire alarm signal system or injures or disables any fire alarm signal box or any part of such system in the vicinity of such building or property, or otherwise prevents an alarm being given

injures or disables any fire alarm signal box or part of the system
otherwise prevents an alarm being given

sound the alarm system required by the state building code

penalties.penalty: Life or any term of not less than 10 years in state prison

penalties.if: the person, after being convicted of any offence mentioned in this section, commits the like offence or any other of the offences therein mentioned
penalties.penalty: No suspension of sentence or probation

crimes.act: Commits any offense described in this section while armed with a firearm
conditions: The offender is armed with a firearm

penalties.if: the person commits a subsequent such offense
penalties.penalty: Life or any term of years in state prison, but not less than 20 years; sentence shall not be suspended, nor shall he be placed on probation

review.plain: Removing or hiding an insured motor vehicle or trailer, or helping do so, with intent to defraud the insurer is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison, a $500-$5,000 fine, and restitution.
acts: removes or conceals a motor vehicle or trailer belonging to himself or another
aids or abets in such removal or concealment

intent: With intent to defraud the insurer

penalties.penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison, or not less than 1 year nor more than 2½ years in jail or house of correction, and a fine of not less than $500 nor more than $5,000

penalties.if: the person has a prior conviction for this crime
penalties.penalty: Sentence shall not be reduced to less than one year, nor suspended or reduced until one year has been served; not eligible for probation, parole, furlough or work release

consequences: Ordered to make restitution to the insurer for any financial loss sustained, after an evidentiary hearing on damages, in addition to incarceration or fine; restitution shall not be ordered to a party aggrieved without that party's consent
Whenever possible, the fine shall equal twice the amount of damages or financial loss suffered
A defendant who defaults on restitution shall be held in contempt unless he made a good faith effort to pay
A prosecution shall not be placed on file, or continued without a finding

On a second or subsequent offense, the commissioner of correction may grant a temporary release in custody only to attend the funeral of next of kin or spouse, visit a critically ill close relative or spouse, or obtain emergency medical services unavailable at the institution
